title: One row on the langar floor
hook: caste, gender and race do not measure the soul
carry: the same light in every soul

segments.voice: Yesterday, wealth: not evil in itself, only in the clinging and the hoarding. Your line was earned and shared.

A long strip of cloth runs down the floor of a gurdwara hall. People sit on it in a row, shoulder to shoulder. A banker in a good coat. A student with a backpack at her feet. A man who came in off the street because he was hungry. A grandmother who barely speaks the language of the room. Someone walks down the line with a bucket of dal and fills every plate from the same ladle. Nobody's plate is first because of who they are. That row is the pangat, and it's a plain picture of today's idea.
screen: `ONE STRIP OF CLOTH. ONE ROW.` → `THE SAME LADLE FOR EVERY PLATE.` → `PANGAT.`

segments.voice: First, the light. Early on this path you met Guru Nanak's line from Raag Asa; here it is again, in paraphrase: recognize the Lord's light in everyone, and don't ask about caste; in the world beyond, there is no caste. The question a whole society used to sort people, what family were you born into, gets set aside. Not because birth is a secret, but because it measures the wrong thing. Second, a sharp question from a weaver. The Granth keeps the verses of Kabir, a weaver by trade, and in one he turns to a man proud of high birth. In paraphrase: if you are so different, why didn't you come into the world some other way? Everyone arrives the same way. The joke has a point. Third, one human family. In the Akal Ustat, a work Sikhs keep in the Dasam Granth, a line Sikhs quote says, in paraphrase: recognize the whole human race as one. Caste, gender, color, nation: none of them is the scale a soul is weighed on. Fourth, the floor. The Gurus didn't leave this a nice sentence. Sit in the row. Eat from the same pot. Take the ladle and serve whoever is next. In the langar, equality stops being an idea and becomes dinner. And equal souls isn't a claim that everyone is the same. The banker and the hungry man are still different people. The light in each is the same light.
screen: `ASA: SEE THE LIGHT, NOT THE CASTE.` · `KABIR: WE ALL ARRIVE THE SAME WAY.` · `ONE HUMAN RACE.` · `PANGAT: THE TEACHING ON THE FLOOR.` · then, large: `THE SAME LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you tend to rank, a little above you or a little below: a boss, maybe, or someone who serves you lunch. On the in-breath, see their face; on the out-breath, let the ranking drop, the way a coat slips off a chair. Then picture one ordinary way to treat them as an equal: their name used, their eyes met, their opinion asked.
Equal souls. Caste, gender and race don't measure the soul; the same light is in everyone, and the langar row puts it into practice. Today's word.
Your line: the same light in every soul. Not who are they, but where is the light in them. See you tomorrow.
